data.content_ref: inline:SRC_004 abstracts away from the specific material-level thermal-physics of SRC_003 and SRC_002, reducing the nocturnal UHI to a single geometric parameter: the urban canyon sky view factor (SVF). Under this abstraction, SVF acts as a sufficient macro-descriptor that implicitly captures the effect of built density on both radiative trapping and wind suppression, making detailed knowledge of material heat capacity or vegetation cover unnecessary for first-order cross-city prediction. This abstraction is REFUTED IF two cities with identical SVF distributions exhibit materially different nocturnal UHI magnitudes due to large differences in construction materials (e.g., a heavy-masonry city vs. a lightweight-wood city) or in irrigation extent, proving that SVF alone is an insufficient descriptor and that the abstracted-out lower-level mechanisms are necessary for accurate prediction.
